playback.legend: Water at Avra Valley Rd & Brawley Wash — Nov 1, 3:00 PM MST · step 21 of 570.030.330.983.36.613noneAverage water depth in the model’s cells, in feet. Grey means the model has no result there — not dry, not safe.↑Blobs move about 0.05 ft per second; the blobs themselves are drifting toward the north.A simulation of the saved model’s water — never a measurement of water on the road.A simulation of this model’s saved water, not a measurement of water on the road.Where these numbers come fromThe blobs are a small water simulation run here in your browser, started from the depth and water level this model saved.Direction comes from the saved run itself: it records how much water crosses each cell edge and which way, at Nov 1, 3:00 PM MST. Speed is worked out from that crossing rate and the model's own water depth — the run does not store a speed, so treat the numbers as derived rather than measured.Saved model run refined-full-41344983607; frozen replay, not current weather.2,048 water blobs, drawn about 33.1 ft across so they can be seen (the water each one stands for is about 3.08 ft). That is a drawing size, not a droplet and not a shoreline.The streaks show which way the water is going. They are drawn at a fixed length — the speed is the number above, not the streak.Seeded from 16041.1 cu ft of model water that its own terrain supports inside this junction.Largest blob move in the last step: 4.770 ft.Two separate numbers: the blobs move about 0.05 ft per second, while their net drift is only about 0.03 ft per second — blobs going opposite ways inside the junction cancel each other out in that second figure. Net drift is the simulation settling, not the saved run's direction; that one comes from the edge crossings and is what the streaks show.10,660 baked triangles of source terrain and road here.Ground photo: USGS/USDA NAIP orthophoto, acquisition date unknown.Placement checked against the live map projection: within 0.002 ft.The ground away from this crossing is the coarse whole-area surface; only the crossing itself is close-up terrain.Simulation step 94.6 ms on this device, 1 per frame, 27 skipped to protect the map.Road width here is a map class default, not a survey. No bridge clearance is assumed.

fluid.boundaryMeaning: Closed bounded junction; dry/missing/native-water support is impermeable; no inferred inlet or discharge

closedTank.lateralBoundary: closed; flux enters through prescribed native perimeter faces
closedTank.meaning: The grid itself stays closed on all sides, as upstream. Water crosses the junction through the native perimeter faces, where the saved run's own signed discharge prescribes the face velocity directly. Nothing is drained toward an invented outside pressure.

fluid.discretisation: Divergence, the pressure Poisson stencil and the gradient subtraction all use the real world metres per cell on each axis. Velocity is world metres per second, so on this 42:1 shallow grid a unit-cell operator would be wrong by that factor.
fluid.surfaceMeaning: Free surface is found by the particles between the measured bed and the native water surface plus a declared 0.06 m illustrative excursion; the native surface remains the risk reference

openBoundary.meaning: Share of the live water sitting within one horizontal cell of the box edge. A boundary that manufactured a pressure head would pull the water against the edge and empty the interior, so this is how the open edge is judged.

sourceDrivenMotion.meaning: Water in cells the saved run gives a velocity for, measured against what it says, and separately the water it says nothing about, which is not driven at all

velocityInitialisation.meaning: Initial particle velocities reconstructed from the saved run's own internal edge discharges; depth-averaged and derived, never a native point velocity

sourceFlowField.meaning: Horizontal grid velocity is relaxed toward the saved run's own reconstructed depth-averaged cell velocity at 1.5 per second, only where that reconstruction exists. It is a relaxation the pressure solve still works against, not an imposed speed, and it is derived from unit discharge rather than a native point velocity.

flow.momentumMeaning: Injected particles carry their own inflow edge's reconstructed depth-averaged velocity, written to that particle's texel only; every other particle keeps its evolved solver velocity
flow.netStorageMeaning: Net storage moves in whole particles: the residual is exactly the held slots (released by outflow, not yet retaken by inflow) plus the sub-particle native net not yet carried. Neither part is topped up with fabricated mass
flow.coupling: Each perimeter edge spends only its own accrued native volume at its own supported cells. Unsupported edges keep their own discrepancy and are never re-drawn onto another edge. Motion between edges is the solver's own pressure response.

phoneMotion.window: fixed simulated-time window on the solver's own clock; generation changes excluded by identity

blobs.rendering: fullscreen particle-derived water surface with written fragment depth; the instanced spheres remain as its capture source
blobs.sizing: display size: at least 5 screen pixels, capped at 5.5 m
blobs.travel: direction only, drawn at a fixed screen length; the measured speed is reported separately
